ruling.recommended_action: Suspend automated handling; refer to RydeHELP human reviewer as a suspected SAFE-1 abuse case (driver told rider to "shut up and let me drive" [F9]) and as a route-deviation/fare case: verify the 09:00–09:11 off-route segment, issue a SAFE-1 conduct warning or account action to the driver, and keep the $7.83 excess-distance issue pending the outcome.
ruling.reasoning:
SAFETY SCREEN (must be done first, and it decides this case). Chat #2 at 09:05: driver: "Shut up and let me drive." [F9], sent in response to the rider's civil routing question [F8]. This is hostile, abusive language aimed at the other party — telling the other party to shut up — which Ryde's code of conduct bars as "abuse of any kind"; the words are read in context and they were not a pickup arrangement or a routing instruction. Under the screen I do not rule on the merits: ruling = escalate, safety_concern = "suspected", based on [F9] (SAFE-1). The rider also states she "felt unsafe" in the complaint; that is noted as context but the concrete basis is the recorded message. No threat, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears beyond this, so SAFE-2 is not engaged; no separate flag_account is ordered, as the safety escalation is the human reviewer's to action.

Note on the escalation result: because safety takes the case out of automated adjudication, no refund is executed here. Had SAFE-1 not applied, the merits point the other way: this is a RydeTAXI trip, so distance is metered (F7 shows distance $30.22 on 21.43 km → $1.4102/km, per km rate = fare.distance_km rate) and the excess distance was billed at $7.83 (5.55 km) [F4]. The off-route segment 09:00–09:11 added 5.14 km [F3] and is not exempt: there is no rider request for a stop or route (the only rider message is a question, [F8]), the driver's "GPS rerouted" claim [F11] is a statement not a record, and the traffic facts show no incident anywhere near the route [F14] — bands 4/5 on PIE/KALLANG PAYA LEBAR [F12][F13] are only supporting evidence and never exempt on their own, and in any event they show moderate speeds, not a blocked optimal route. Under RD-2 the partial refund would be 5.14 km × $1.4102 = $7.25 (rounded), with the residual map-matching/loop distance (5.55 − 5.14) not refunded. That is provided for the human reviewer only; it is not the operative ruling. The waiting fee of $0.11 [F5] is a metered waiting unit on a RydeTAXI trip and stands under RD-3(c).
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety screen triggered: recorded driver message telling the rider to "shut up" [F9] is abuse under SAFE-1; safety_concern = suspected. No automated ruling or refund is issued; case goes to a human reviewer, who should also consider the unexempted 5.14 km off-route segment [F3] and the $7.83 excess-distance billing [F4] (potential RD-2 partial refund of $7.25 at $1.4102/km) once the conduct matter is handled.

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 09:00–09:11 drove 6.89 km where the optimal route covers 1.75 km, adding 5.14 km [F3]. No rider stop/route request exists — the only rider message is a question about the route [F8] — so nothing exempts it under RD-3 or RD-5, and the driver's post-trip claim that the GPS rerouted [F11] is a statement, not consent and not a record. No traffic incident near the route [F14]; the PIE/Kallang speed bands 5 and 4 [F12][F13] are moderate speeds on different roads and in any event serve only as corroboration, never a standalone exemption (RD-4(b)). Segment counts under RD-1/RD-2; the amount would be 5.14 × $1.4102 = $7.25, but no refund executes because the case is escalated for a SAFE-1 concern.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip statement that 'I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted' is a statement, not a system record; GPS shows a 5.14 km off-route segment with no traffic incident near the route [F3][F14], so the reroute claim does not provide a reasonable cause under RD-4. It also cannot supply rider consent: consent must be the rider's own message sent before the detour began (RD-5), and no such message exists.
Traffic facts show only speed bands 4–5 on PIE/Kallang [F12][F13] and explicitly no incidents near the route [F14]; band evidence alone never exempts a segment (RD-4(b)).

safety_basis: F9 driver chat: "Shut up and let me drive." — hostile/abusive language directed at the rider in reply to her routing question [F8]; Ryde code of conduct bars abuse of any kind (SAFE-1).
Complaint states the rider 'felt unsafe' after the driver's response; escalated for a human reviewer.
